metadata.subject: Algorithms
metadata.title: Discover Merge Sort
metadata.description: Divide an array into smaller parts, then merge sorted halves into order.

learning_objectives: Split an array into smaller halves.
Merge sorted halves by choosing the smaller front value.

mission.title: Divide then merge
mission.description: Watch Merge Sort split the work and combine sorted pieces.

introduction.title: Merge Sort divides before it sorts
introduction.content: Merge Sort breaks an array into smaller pieces, sorts those pieces, and merges them back together in order.
points: Small pieces are easier to order.
The merge compares the front of each sorted half.
The final merge creates one sorted array.

worked_example.title: Split and merge
worked_example.content: First divide the array, then choose the smaller front value while merging.

steps.explanation: Compare the fronts and repeatedly take the smaller value.

worked_example.conclusion: Divide and conquer turns one large sort into smaller sorts plus an ordered merge.

next.title: Now build the merge yourself.
next.content: Choose the split, then select each smallest front value.

next-step: The array was divided into two balanced pieces.
You selected the next value for the sorted left half.
The left half is sorted, so now build the right half.
You selected the next value for the sorted right half.
Both halves are sorted and ready to merge.
The smaller front value entered the merged array.
Keep comparing the two front values.
The merge is nearly finished; take the last available front value.

quiz.question: What does Merge Sort do before merging values?
options: Divides the array into smaller parts

discovery.title: Merge Sort discovery
discovery.summary: Merge Sort solves smaller pieces first, then combines them by repeatedly selecting the smaller front value.

sections.title: What?
sections.content: Merge Sort uses divide and conquer: split the array, sort pieces, then merge them.

sections.title: Example
sections.content: [8, 3, 6, 2] splits into [8, 3] and [6, 2], then merges to [2, 3, 6, 8].

sections.title: Why?
sections.content: Smaller sorted halves make the final merge predictable and efficient.

sections.title: Remember
sections.content: Split → sort halves → take the smaller front value while merging.

alternate_explanations.title: Think of two sorted queues
alternate_explanations.content: Compare the person at the front of two ordered lines and let the smaller one leave first.

alternate_explanations.title: Walk through it
alternate_explanations.content: Merge [3, 8] and [2, 6]: take 2, then 3, then 6, then 8.

recall.title: Recall
recall.prompt: In your own words, why does Merge Sort split the array before merging it?
recall.model_answer: Splitting creates small pieces that can be sorted easily; comparing the fronts of sorted pieces makes the final merge orderly.
